subject: ZenithAI TCO post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@zenith.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@zenith.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: ZenithAI — TCO post-call recap and next steps

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for the conversation today — really helpful to learn more about the annotation pipeline and where latency + unit cost are driving your ops spend. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and to capture next steps: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Current setup: running a nightly batch of 250k calls + 24/7 inference for low-latency features at peak, ~70% of calls are short (<= 120 tokens) but tail goes to 4k tokens for complex QA.
- Pain: token spend is spiking month-to-month and unpredictable; on-prem infra has frequent cold-start latency and KV-cache misses for shared contexts.
- Goal: reduce per-request unit cost by 30–50% while preserving 95th % latency SLAs for low-latency features. Evaluate Dedicated vs Private for predictable pricing and data controls.

Preliminary TCO levers discussed
- Intelligent batching: 10–20% token-cost reduction on peak throughput paths via request coalescing (we estimate ~12% savings given your latency SLOs).
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts: can reduce token decoding and compute by ~25% on cached requests (high ROI for short recurring prompts).
- Quantization + memory-optimized kernels for long-tail QA: 15–25% GPU cost reduction with minimal quality impact (we’ll validate on your eval set).
- Model routing: route low-cost/fast variant for short prompts and reserve large variant for long-context queries — expected blended unit cost drop ~30%.

High-level annualized cost estimate (back-of-envelope)
- Baseline (current): ~$1.2M/year (inferred from your usage snapshot).
- Optimized (with batching/caching + routing + quant): ~$700–850k/year.
- Expected payback: ~6–9 months assuming conservative adoption of caching & routing.

Attachments
- I’ve attached the usage snapshot you shared and a Redwood TCO workbook (redwood-tco-workbook.xlsx) with model-by-workload line items and assumptions we used for the estimate.

Next steps
1) I’ll send the TCO workbook filled with the assumptions we used (attached). Please confirm any incorrect assumptions (e.g., average tokens per call).
2) Rafael to join a pricing deep-dive next Tue (23 Feb) to go line-by-line on Dedicated vs Private pricing.
3) You to share the 7-day production trace (subset) and any SLOs by route — we’ll run a quick prefix-cache simulation.

Would you be available for 60 minutes on Tue 23 Feb at 10am PT for the pricing deep-dive? If not, suggest alternatives.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ZenithAI — TCO post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — very thorough and helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we dive into the workbook: 

1) The baseline you used — does that include our current on-prem amortized infra costs? We only uploaded the API-level usage snapshot (tokens + counts), not CAPEX.
2) For the prefix/KV caching savings: are you assuming a cold-start hit on every container restart? Our infra has ~20% churn during peak deploys.

Happy to do Tue 10am PT — Priya and I are good for that slot. We’ll try to pull a 7-day trace slice to share by EOD Monday.

On (1) — if CapEx isn’t included, can you provide a blended infra+cloud number so we can compare apples-to-apples?

- Samir
Director of ML Platform
Zenith AI

Subject: Re: ZenithAI — TCO post-call recap and next steps

Samir — good questions, short answers below and we’ll dig into the line items on Tue: 

1) Baseline: the workbook includes an "API-level" baseline (tokens x model unit cost + estimated cloud GPU run-hours). It does not include historical CAPEX amortization for your on-prem GPU fleet. We can add a blended row — please share either (a) monthly amortized $ or (b) per-GPU hourly equivalent and we’ll fold it into the model.

2) Caching assumptions: the workbook scenario assumes warm caches for 70% of repeated contexts and models a 2–3% cold-start penalty during container churn. If your churn is 20% we’ll model a higher cold-start hit — that will reduce the near-term savings but caching still shows positive ROI for short prompts.

Action items I’ll own before Tue:
- Update workbook with a blended infra row if you send the amortized CAPEX number.
- Run a quick cache-simulation against the 7-day slice once received and report expected token and compute savings.

Thanks — Marissa

Looping in from Redwood pricing — happy to join Tue’s call. Quick note on the Dedicated vs Private comparison we'll cover: 
- Dedicated: predictable monthly committed capacity; cost benefits when sustained throughput > X tokens/sec. Easier procurement (monthly invoice).
- Private: better for regulated data and predictable long-tail costs if you can amortize CAPEX; larger org-level ops burden but lower per-token compute if you run on your own optimized infra.

On blending infra: if you send per-GPU amortized $/month Rafael and I will produce a blended infra line in the workbook and a short slide summarizing payback and NPV assumptions.

See you Tue 10am PT.
— Rafael
